topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, outlines the structure of the cancer lecture course, and sets out the lecture's learning objectives.

topics.label: Nature of Cancer and Epidemiological Evidence for Environmental Causes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease influenced by the microenvironment and evaluate the balance between intrinsic random mutations and environmental exposures through epidemiological data.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Carcinogenesis: Mutagens, Promoters, and Host Factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the cellular and molecular mechanisms through which pathogens, chemical mutagens, xenobiotic metabolism, tumor promoters, and host developmental susceptibility drive carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methodologies for Determining and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the complementary genomic, epidemiological, in vivo animal, and in vitro experimental methodologies used to identify and verify carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecture concludes with a summary of the main themes and a discussion of risk-benefit assessment in everyday exposure decisions.
